name: ESP32 Power Management
description: The `esp32_power_management` platform turns on ESP-IDF power management. It scales the CPU frequency between a minimum and a maximum depending on what the running components need, and it can put the chip into automatic light sleep whenever nothing is scheduled to run. Both work on the ESP-IDF and the Arduino framework.

config_entries.label: Enable Light Sleep
config_entries.description: Enter light sleep automatically whenever no task is runnable, which also stops the periodic tick interrupt while idle. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Idle Time Before Sleep
config_entries.description: How many FreeRTOS ticks (1 ms each, as ESPHome runs the ESP32 tick at 1 kHz) the system must stay idle before it enters light sleep. Minimum `2`. Defaults to `3`.

config_entries.label: Max Frequency
config_entries.description: The CPU frequency used while a component holds a CPU lock. Must be one of the frequencies the chip supports (for example `80MHz`, `160MHz` or `240MHz` on the ESP32, and `16MHz`, `32MHz`, `48MHz`, `64MHz` or `96MHz` on the ESP32-H2). Defaults to the `cpu_frequency` of the [`esp32`](https://esphome.io/components/esp32/) component. A different value is accepted; validation logs that the CPU will be clocked down to it, or warns that it may run above the boot frequency under load.

config_entries.label: Min Frequency
config_entries.description: The CPU frequency used while no CPU lock is held. Must divide the crystal frequency (`40MHz` on most variants, `32MHz` on the ESP32-H2) or be one of the CPU frequencies, be at least `10MHz` on the ESP32 and `2MHz` on the other variants, and be no higher than the maximum. Defaults to the crystal frequency, limited to the maximum.

config_entries.label: Power Down Flash
config_entries.description: Power down the flash chip during light sleep. Requires `enable_light_sleep` and is rejected when the device has PSRAM. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Power Down Peripherals
config_entries.description: Save and restore the peripheral registers around light sleep so the peripherals themselves can be powered down. Only available on chips with a TOP power domain (ESP32-C5, C6, C61, H2, H4, H21, P4 and S31), where it defaults to `true` when light sleep is enabled. Requires `enable_light_sleep`.

config_entries.label: Profiling
config_entries.description: Record how long each power management lock is held and how much time the chip spends in each power state, for the lock dump described below. It costs some runtime overhead, so leave it off in production. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Trace
config_entries.description: Signal power management events (ticks, frequency changes, entering and leaving idle) on a set of GPIOs, as listed in ESP-IDF's [`pm_trace.c`](https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf/blob/master/components/esp_pm/pm_trace.c). Those pins are taken over, so this is for analysing the behaviour on a bench only. Defaults to `false`.
